questions.question: Why is `State.messages` annotated with `add_messages` in the graph definition?
options: It encrypts messages before they are written to `MemorySaver`
It converts a list of messages into one string before the model sees it
It appends and reconciles new message updates instead of overwriting the conversation list
It routes every message directly to the `tools` node without consulting the agent
questions.explanation: LangGraph uses the field reducer to merge node updates. `add_messages` appends and reconciles message objects instead of overwriting earlier human, assistant, or tool messages; it does not perform tool routing.

questions.question: What does `should_continue` return when the last assistant message contains a nonempty `tool_calls` list?
options: `END`, because tool calls are terminal output from the agent node
`agent`, which invokes the model again before any tool can run
`interrupt`, a special node name created automatically by the checkpointer
`tools`, routing execution to the `ToolNode`
questions.explanation: The router checks `getattr(last, "tool_calls", None)`. A truthy list returns `tools`; a message without tool calls returns `END`, so the graph either executes tools or finishes.

questions.question: What is the observable effect of compiling with `interrupt_before=["tools"]`?
options: The graph pauses before executing the pending tool call, so its side effect can be approved or denied
The `tools` node is removed from the graph and tool calls are returned as plain text
Execution pauses after the tool has run, allowing a reviewer to undo its side effect
Only the first message is checkpointed; later nodes run without persistence
questions.explanation: `interrupt_before=["tools"]` suspends execution before `ToolNode` runs. The pending call and checkpointed state can be inspected before any tool side effect, then the same thread can be resumed explicitly.

questions.question: Why does the demo choose `history[-1].config` as its earliest checkpoint before the time-travel branch?
options: The final snapshot always contains the user's first message by definition of `StateGraph`
`get_state_history` yields snapshots newest first, so `history[-1]` is the oldest available snapshot
Only the last snapshot has a valid thread ID; earlier configs are read-only copies
LangGraph stores history alphabetically by node name, making the last item the initial node
questions.explanation: In this demo, `get_state_history` yields snapshots newest first. Therefore `history[-1]` is the oldest available checkpoint, which is the state selected before adding the alternate math question; this is an ordering property, not a guarantee about the first user message.

questions.question: What does `app.stream(Command(resume=True), config, stream_mode="updates")` do after the tools interrupt?
options: It clears the checkpointer and starts a new thread with no messages
It rewinds to the first checkpoint and discards the pending tool call
It resumes the paused thread and runs the pending tool
It asks the model for a new user message before any state transition
questions.explanation: `Command(resume=True)` continues the same `thread_id` from the interrupt. The tool call is executed, its result is appended through the message reducer, and control returns to the agent node.

questions.question: What happens when the demo's `calculator` tool receives `2 + unknown`?
options: It imports the missing name from Python's global namespace and returns a value
It returns the literal expression because the graph does not execute tools in tests
It asks `web_lookup` to define `unknown` before evaluating the expression
It returns `ERROR: only digits and + - * / ( ) are allowed` before calling `eval`
questions.explanation: `calculator` checks the character allowlist before evaluating. Because `unknown` contains letters, the guard returns `ERROR: only digits and + - * / ( ) are allowed`; execution never reaches `eval` or a `NameError` handler.
